prompt:
add three things to logstat (this repo). usage becomes `logstat [--since TS] [--json] [--top-sources N] <file>`, flags in any order. no new dependencies, keep the existing unit tests passing.

- `--since TS`: TS is an RFC3339 timestamp, e.g. `2026-03-14T09:15:02Z` or with a `+HH:MM`/`-HH:MM` offset, whole seconds. only count lines whose timestamp is >= TS (compare instants). unparsable TS: message on stderr, exit 2.
- `--top-sources N`: N is a positive integer, else exit 2. after the counts, print `source count` for the N most frequent sources among counted lines, sorted by count descending then name ascending. source = the text before the colon, so `auth` in `INFO  auth: user signed in`.
- `--json`: print one line and nothing else: `{"counts":{"ERROR":3,"WARN":7},"total":10,"first":"<ts>","last":"<ts>","skipped":0}`. keys in exactly that order. `counts` has only nonzero levels, in ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG order (`{}` if none). `total` = counted lines. `first`/`last` = the timestamp as written in the file, of the earliest/latest counted line by time; `null` when nothing counted. with `--top-sources`, add `"sources":[["auth",5],["db",2]]` after `last`. `skipped` is always present.
- malformed lines are skipped and counted in `skipped`, with or without --since. a line is valid only if it is `<timestamp> <LEVEL> <source>: <message>` with LEVEL exactly ERROR, WARN, INFO or DEBUG and a non-empty source (fields separated by whitespace). blank lines are ignored, not counted. lines dropped by --since are not skipped. text output (no --json) ends with `SKIPPED n` when n > 0.

without the new flags the text output is unchanged: `ERROR 3`, `WARN 7`, `INFO 120`, one per line, zero levels omitted. every output line ends with a newline. examples/sample.log has a sample.
